story_type: rocket booster test with an anomaly
hook: Fifteen seconds before the end, pieces started flying
narration: Fifteen seconds before the end of this rocket test, pieces started flying.
This is a new booster for NASA's Moon rocket, strapped down on its side in the Utah desert.
It was the first full-scale ground test of this new five-segment motor.
Once lit, it pushed out three point nine million pounds of thrust.
A solid rocket motor can't be throttled or switched off. Once it starts, it burns until the fuel is gone.
So when something went wrong near the end, the burn just kept going.
[short pause] NASA called it an abnormal event. The motor fired for more than two minutes in all.
outcome: Even so, NASA met several of the test's main goals and got valuable data on the risks.
title: Moon rocket booster test goes wrong
question_comment: Would you call this test a failure or a success?

facts.claim: Fired horizontally at Promontory, Utah, June 26
facts.source_quote: Secured horizontally in a test stand at Northrop Grumman’s test facility in Promontory, Utah, the single five-segment booster motor fired for more than two minutes and produced 3.9 million pounds of thrust.

facts.claim: First full-scale ground test of new five-segment motor
facts.source_quote: This test was the first full-scale ground test of a new five-segment solid rocket motor.

facts.claim: Abnormal event about 15 seconds before the end
facts.source_quote: During the test, there was an abnormal event approximately 15 seconds before the end of the motor firing.

facts.claim: Outcome: objectives met and data received
facts.source_quote: Despite this event, NASA achieved several of the test’s primary objectives and received valuable data on technical risks identified ahead of the test.

description:
NASA and Northrop Grumman fired a new five-segment solid rocket booster for the Space Launch System in Promontory, Utah, on June 26, 2025. An abnormal event happened about 15 seconds before the end of the two-minute firing, and NASA still met several of the test's primary objectives.
